Simulate a 2D lid-driven cavity flow using the OpenFOAM icoFoam solver for transient incompressible laminar flow.
The cavity is a square domain of 0.1 m × 0.1 m in the x-y plane, extruded 0.01 m in the z direction.
The top wall (y = 0.1 m) moves to the right (+x direction) at a constant velocity of 1 m/s.
The left, right, and bottom walls are stationary with no-slip (zero velocity) boundary conditions.
The front and back faces (z = 0 and z = 0.01 m) use "empty" boundary conditions to enforce 2D behavior.
The fluid is incompressible with a kinematic viscosity of 0.001 m²/s, yielding a Reynolds number of Re = 100.
The initial condition is a quiescent fluid: zero velocity and zero pressure everywhere in the domain at t = 0.
The grid is a uniform Cartesian mesh of 20 × 20 × 1 cells (block definition 20×20×1).
The simulation is time-accurate and transient, running from startTime = 0 to endTime = 0.5 s with a fixed timestep deltaT = 0.002 s.
Results are written every 20 timesteps (writeControl: timeStep, writeInterval: 20), corresponding to output every 0.04 s, yielding 25 output frames that capture the development of the primary recirculation vortex.
All other settings follow the standard icoFoam defaults for a laminar incompressible case on a uniform Cartesian grid.
